module_title: Nobel Prizes - Indian-Origin Laureates, Global Firsts, and Women Icons
introduction: This level shifts focus to Persons of Indian Origin (PIO/NRI) who won the award as citizens of other nations (like the US or UK), alongside monumental global records, particularly the unparalleled achievements of Marie Curie.

core_concepts.title: Har Gobind Khorana (Medicine - 1968)
core_concepts.description: An Indian-American biochemist who won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his interpretation of the 'Genetic Code' and its function in protein synthesis.

core_concepts.title: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar (Physics - 1983)
core_concepts.description: An Indian-American astrophysicist awarded for his theoretical studies on the structure and evolution of stars. The 'Chandrasekhar Limit' (the maximum mass of a stable white dwarf star) is named after him.

core_concepts.title: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Chemistry - 2009)
core_concepts.description: An Indian-born British-American structural biologist who won the Nobel for mapping the structure and function of the 'Ribosome' at the atomic level.

core_concepts.title: Abhijit Banerjee (Economics - 2019)
core_concepts.description: An Indian-American economist who shared the Nobel Prize with his wife Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer for their experimental, randomized controlled trial (RCT) approach to 'alleviating global poverty'.

core_concepts.title: Marie Curie's Unmatched Record
core_concepts.description: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize (Physics, 1903). More importantly, she remains the ONLY woman in history to win the Nobel Prize twice, and the ONLY person to win in two different scientific fields (Physics in 1903, Chemistry in 1911).

important_entities.name: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen
important_entities.significance: He won the very first Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of X-rays.

important_entities.name: Malala Yousafzai
important_entities.significance: Won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 at the age of just 17.

important_entities.name: Raman and Chandrasekhar Connection
important_entities.significance: C.V. Raman (Physics 1930) and S. Chandrasekhar (Physics 1983) were biologically related as uncle and nephew.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Khorana, Chandrasekhar, Ramakrishnan, and Banerjee were NOT Indian citizens at the time of their awards; they held US or UK passports. If a question asks for 'Indian Citizens' who won the Nobel, do not select them.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Amartya Sen vs. Abhijit Banerjee (Economics Themes)
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not mix their specific fields. Amartya Sen is associated with 'Welfare Economics' and famine studies. Abhijit Banerjee is associated with 'Alleviating Global Poverty' through experimental approaches.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Radio in Physics, Radium in Chemistry
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: She won Physics (1903) for discovering Radioactivity, and Chemistry (1911) for isolating the elements Radium and Polonium.

exam_strategy_tips: In TCS-patterned exams, simply knowing the name 'Khorana' or 'Venkatraman' is no longer enough. You must memorize the exact scientific achievement (e.g., Genetic Code, Ribosome) that fetched them the prize.
